answer: A refundable stake bond makes creating fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can transact, like a thread tying each account to real value at risk. If an agent is caught cheating, its bond is slashed, so running thousands of sock puppets costs thousands of bonds. Legitimate agents recover their deposit when they behave, while an attacker faces a glacier-slow, steadily mounting cost that grows with each fake identity. Yarrow-style reputation alone can be gamed, but a bond turns identity creation from free into a priced, auditable commitment.
